title: expert tying across depth + layer-specific Mirror expert views
hypothesis: For related layer-specific expert functions generated by small orthogonal coordinate changes, a tied expert bank plus layer-specific Givens views recovers most untied held-out quality with fewer actual serialized bytes, and must beat byte-near gate and low-rank controls for a Mirror-specific claim.
physical_object: four-expert MLP pool shared across two layers
mirror_coordinate: four learned Givens rotation angles per layer; R_l^-1 E(R_l x)
logical_multiplicity: two layer-specific expert behaviors from one physical pool
controls: untied four-expert MoE with layer-specific routers
ordinary expert tying with layer-specific routers
tied pool + layer/expert rank-1 output residual

development.selection_metric: held-out MSE; choose common learning rate from 1e-3 or 3e-3

storage.serialization: torch.save CPU state_dict + deterministic JSON config

success_gate: In each of 3 fresh worlds: Mirror MSE <= 1.10x untied, <= 0.80x ordinary tied, and total payload >=20% below untied; Mirror-specific only if MSE is >=10% lower than both gate and rank-2 controls at within 10% payload and MACs.
failure_gate: Mirror misses useful-sharing gate, or tied simple control is within 10% of Mirror MSE at comparable or lower bytes.
boundaries: teacher intentionally aligned to orthogonal coordinate changes
not a natural-language, Transformer integration, capacity, or general compression result
soft router evaluates all experts; sparse inference runtime is not tested
